clue.text: One who raised Cain about fuel and transport in foreign location

indicators.note: about signals turning the father's name round so it reads backwards

parts.note: in Genesis Adam was the father of Cain, so he raised him
gas is a fuel
a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A biblical troublemaker's minder fusses over fuel and vehicles somewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised Cain' suggests causing trouble, but here it is literal parenting; 'about' turns ADAM into MADA.
explanation.definitionFit: The island off Africa is a place foreign to a British solver, so a foreign location.

clue.text: Endless cry of terror, grabbed by fresh villain

indicators.note: grabbed by puts the shortened cry inside the word for fresh

parts.note: mint condition means fresh and new

indicators.note: Endless signals removing the final letter of the cry

parts.note: a scream is a cry of terror

explanation.surface: A villain is seized by fear, letting out an unending scream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' looks like an adjective for villain but supplies the outer letters; 'Endless' removes the cry's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer, a synonym for a villain.

clue.text: Writer is under attack having overturned first of theories

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits under another, so it comes after it
in a down clue overturned means the word for attack is read from bottom up

parts.note: a raid is an attack

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word theories

explanation.surface: An author finds themselves criticised after their ideas are knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'under' means the second piece follows the first, and 'overturned' reads the attack word upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps a diary writes regularly, so is a kind of writer.

clue.text: Evil act in a mostly Communist town

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: Trot is short for Trotskyist, a kind of Communist
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Something wicked happens in a town run largely by Communists.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrocity is a shockingly wicked deed, an evil act.

clue.text: Construction Kit?

parts.note: read not as a toy box but as a builder called Kit, the familiar short form of Christopher, the great English architect of St Paul's Cathedral

explanation.surface: A box of parts for building models.
explanation.definitionFit: The architect of St Paul's was famous for construction, and Kit is a pet form of his first name.

clue.text: Screw up, and plan afresh

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: screw is slang for a prison warder

explanation.surface: Make a mess of a design and start drawing it again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw' is prison slang for a warder, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraw is to draw again, which is to plan afresh.

clue.text: Pounds stuffed into sack in violent robbery

indicators.note: stuffed into puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a sack is a bag
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A thief crams money into a bag during a brutal heist.
explanation.definitionFit: Blag is British slang for a robbery, especially a violent one.

clue.text: Drug restriction took effect on a certain person

parts.note: a bar is a restriction
bit is past tense of bite, as when brakes or a policy take effect
one means a certain person, as in one who knows

explanation.surface: A ban on a drug started to work on one particular individual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is a link word here; 'took effect' is the past of bite, as brakes bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbitone is a sedative drug, an early barbiturate.

clue.text: A royal servant keeps an arrangement for prince?

indicators.note: keeps means holds another piece inside

parts.note: a page is a boy servant at a royal court

explanation.surface: A palace page holds onto a deal made on behalf of a prince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangement' looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the definition; the question mark flags the loose sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An apanage is land or income granted to a younger prince for his upkeep, a provision made for him.

clue.text: Meet more courteous-sounding traveller

indicators.note: sounding signals the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: meet is see, as in to see someone, and more courteous is fairer, giving see fairer

explanation.surface: Encountering someone more polite on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: SEE (meet) plus FAIRER (more courteous) is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafarer is a sailor, someone who travels by sea.

clue.text: African city finally welcomed pope

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word welcomed

parts.note: Urban is a name taken by several popes

explanation.surface: An African city eventually gave a warm welcome to the Pontiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Durban is a major port city in South Africa.

clue.text: Manage to get round current financial hardship

indicators.note: to get round means to surround another piece

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Trying to cope with present money troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present' but is I, the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin is the loss of all one's money, extreme financial hardship.

clue.text: Foreign sailor captured by Napoleon? Not right

indicators.note: captured by means held inside another piece
Not signals leaving out the letter that follows

parts.note: Napoleon was born in Corsica, so he is an example of a Corsican
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A foreign seaman was taken prisoner by Napoleon, which was wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not right' drops R from the islander; the question mark marks Napoleon as an example of a Corsican.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the Central American country is foreign to a British reader.

clue.text: Order given on parade in a situation of hostility, say

indicators.note: say signals the phrase is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: at tension means in a state of hostility, said much like the answer

explanation.surface: A command shouted on the parade ground amid a tense standoff.
explanation.definitionFit: Attention is the drill command telling soldiers to stand upright and still.

clue.text: Young assistant working in yonder bar

indicators.note: working signals the letters are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A young helper employed in the bar over there.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand boy is a youth employed to run errands, a young assistant.

clue.text: Hat left abandoned in shady retreat

indicators.note: abandoned signals the letter for left is dropped

parts.note: a bowler is a hat

explanation.surface: A hat left behind in a shady garden spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' is L, removed from BOWLER, not a past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: A bower is a leafy, shaded garden shelter.

clue.text: Hiding one's true feelings about media journalist

parts.note: re means about, concerning
the press means the news media
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist conceals emotions when talking about the media.
explanation.definitionFit: Repressed describes someone who keeps their emotions bottled up.

clue.text: Compiles various arguments

indicators.note: various signals the letters are set out in different order

explanation.surface: Someone collects a range of debating points.
explanation.definitionFit: Polemics are forceful written or spoken arguments.

clue.text: Famous actress given lines after short period

indicators.note: after places the lines piece following the shortened period
short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a term is a period of time
RY is short for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A celebrated actress is handed her script after a brief spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' is railway lines, a crossword convention. Ellen Terry was a leading Victorian stage actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen Terry was a famous English Shakespearean actress.

clue.text: Retired thespian, demanding sort

parts.note: ex means former, as one retired
a thespian is an actor

explanation.surface: A retired actor who is hard to please.
explanation.definitionFit: An exactor is one who exacts or demands payment, a demanding person.

clue.text: Distribution of top US home movie of a violent nature?

indicators.note: distribution means the letters are dealt out in a new order

explanation.surface: Releasing a hit American home video full of violence.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoot-em-up is a film or game full of gunfire, so violent in nature.

clue.text: German cooked duck prepared with vegetables and wine

indicators.note: cooked signals the letters are mixed up

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A German chef cooks duck with vegetables and wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' is the cricket zero, O, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken Marengo is a dish cooked with tomatoes, mushrooms and wine; Marengo describes that style.

clue.text: Sexy remark? You must be joking!

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of disbelief, as in surely not

explanation.definitionFit: A come-on is a flirtatious lure, and come on! expresses disbelief.

clue.text: Oceanography classes? A lot to take in

definitions.meaning: lessons about the sea, the main being an old word for the ocean
the biggest dish of a meal, a large amount to eat

explanation.definitionFit: Main is the sea, so lessons on it fit, and the central dish of a meal is plenty to eat.

clue.text: Tortured regularly, indeed

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word Tortured

explanation.surface: Tormented on a routine basis, really.
explanation.definitionFit: True can mean indeed, as in an admission: true, I was there.

clue.text: Secure accommodation for Arabs

definitions.meaning: lodging for horses, Arabs being a breed of horse

explanation.definitionFit: Stable means steady, and a stable houses horses such as Arab thoroughbreds.

clue.text: Fence by side of river in bad shape, beginning to sink

indicators.note: side of picks one edge letter, here the opening one of river

parts.note: ailing means unwell, in bad shape

indicators.note: beginning to picks the opening letter of sink

explanation.surface: A fence beside a river is in poor repair and starting to subside.
explanation.definitionFit: Railings form a fence of upright bars.

clue.text: Show effects of strain in battle

definitions.meaning: to wear thin, as nerves or cloth do under stress

explanation.definitionFit: Nerves or cloth fray under strain, and a fray is a fight.

clue.text: Cannon does prove defective for a short time

indicators.note: defective means broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cannon fails within moments of firing.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanosecond is a billionth of a second, a very short time.
